reviewNotes:
# Four-source intake — September 14, 2026

## Scope and status

Four supplied originals, 228 physical PDF pages: License 9758 (8), Northernaire OSC report (14), Cadillac RI (169), EPA draft injection permit (37). Native text was read in page order and every supplied page was rendered and inspected. Windows OCR was applied to the 169-page RI, License p8 and draft-permit pp27–29,35–36. OCR output is not itself review evidence. Material readings used below were checked against page images. Review coverage is separate from verification and publication.

License and draft permit match existing catalog originals byte-for-byte. The incoming RI differs in bytes but matches the existing 169-page RI on every normalized-text page and every 108-DPI rendered page; see groundwater-comparison.json. Preserve its supplied filename and hash, reuse the canonical original. The RI was already linked in a timeline block but lacked its own source-catalog entry; add that entry without another PDF. The Northernaire report is a new original, not the existing three-page 1985 progress report.

The license and supplied draft permit have complete readable-page coverage. The 14 supplied OSC pages are read, but the listed appendices are absent. The RI has complete page visitation/text review, with unresolved small map labels (especially p53) and dense historical risk-table numeric detail (pp149–150,152–154,157–158,160). Do not mark the complete RI package Strict Fully Verified. Its published hydrogeology findings are supported independently by readable narrative and figures. Missing references/appendices and limited legibility remain open, not silently waived.

## License 9758 — content, not filename

- p1: issued November 19, 2024, expires November 19, 2029; Wexford County Landfill LLC; facility 470336; 196.4 acres. Header metadata has a different facility-number string and is not controlling. Facility address and contact-address ZIP strings differ; preserve rather than normalize without evidence.
- p2: currently authorized active cells total 36.31 acres. Cell I is 10.46 additional financially assured acres, requiring construction certification/approval before waste receipt. Future West cells 1–9 (68.50 acres) are not licensed for operation. Partial closed portions 22.44 acres overlap named cells, not necessarily an accounting error.
- p3: August 7 application revised October 29, 2024; fee $12,500 received August 19. Covenant recorded June 20, 2011, Liber 640 pp659–664. Required financial assurance $22,006,153.35; provided $22,157,990.45. Named instruments are not new cash operating revenue.
- p4: incorporates Construction Permits 4100/4127 and separately identified hydrogeology, RAP, recirculation, lagoon/spray-curtain, engineering, cover, gas and odor plans. The listed documents are retrieval leads, not attached in full here. Repair/re-certification conditions do not prove a liner failure occurred.
- p5: March 2018 hydrogeological monitoring plan; leachate recirculation requires approved plan. Leak-detection action/response rates 5/25 gallons/acre/day are thresholds, not measured leakage. Alternate cover table prints **Cadillac Casing, Inc.** for foundry sand; do not silently change to Casting. Listed allowances: foundry sand unlimited; ash250, auto fluff1650, contaminated soil500, solidified drilling muds300, Norm solids400, solidified solids450, wood chips200, screened compost rejects200, catch-basin solids200, oil-and-gas solids200 tons/month. Permission is not actual receipt.
- p6: alternate cover limited to daily cover, not road/fill uses. October 9, 2007 Limited Residential RAP and October 5 agreement: County DPW responsibilities retained regardless of ownership; LLC owner must also implement RAP and ensure access/performance through contractual arrangements. This assigns responsibilities under this record, not a new liability finding.
- p7: final administrative language. p8 Attachment A, August2024 map: 46.77 active acres includes Cell I's10.46; map's label does not supersede p2's36.31 currently authorized acreage. Partial closure22.44/future68.50/total137.71; facility196.4 acres is a different area definition.

## Northernaire On-Scene Coordinator report — 14 supplied pages

- pp1–3: undated report, CERCLA Immediate Removal Project68-95-007, EPA RegionV, archive209451. Appendix list A–U plus text reference to V; those appendices are not in this14-page file. Event date is derived from narrative, not scan metadata.
- p4:1002SixthStreet, sandy ground, property R.W.Meyer Inc., tenant Northernaire/WillardGarwood; operations1971–April/May1981. October1978 two private wells showed chromium. Report identifies leaking sewer/catch basin; City revoked sewer permit and plugged connection. Continued waste discharge afterwards is explicitly suspected, not established.
- p5: location map. p6: building diagram about100x50ft with numbered process tanks, acid drums, pails, sludge piles, discolored soil, offices, lab, former waste-tank location; numbered inventory refers to absent AppendixQ. North catch basin20ft away. Diagram not to scale.
- p7: March16–17,1983 inspection; no instrument readings with cyanide tubes/explosimeter/HNU; LevelB inspection. Open-bottom, unsealed catch basin allowed seepage; as soil saturated, second pipe drained northeast into EighthStreet sanitary sewer and City sewage treatment plant. Federal removal initiated July5,1983; characterization sampling ended July8. July11 decontamination rinse hauled to Nelson Industrial Services, Detroit. This is not proof of a measured historical volume received by WWTP.
- p8: acids to Nelson; cyanide liquids Envirite, HarveyIL; cyanide sludge solidified/drummed to CECOS/CER near Cincinnati; sewer excavation; prior MDNR hydrogeology order1978 and unfunded1979plan. ClassIII material went to an unnamed local landfill (also p12), not identified as Wexford.
- p9 disposal table, checked visually:7/20/83 acid3450gal Nelson MI0325954;7/28 cyanide4000gal Envirite MI0328354/IL0820917;7/29 cyanide1402gal Envirite **MI032853 as printed**, IL0816932;8/1 cyanide mixture66drums InlandWaters→CECOS/CER MI0328357;8/2 hypochlorite5000gal Nelson MI0328355;8/3 cyanide70drums MI0328358 and14drums MI0317213 InlandWaters→CECOS/CER. Table entries are report-level manifest summaries; original manifests in absent AppendixI remain needed.
- p10 narrative total $156,171.58. Contractor subtotal $142,041.02: labor45,489.39;materials14,399.30;equipment33,432.05;subcontracts48,720.28. Subcontracts:RustyJohnson3364.34,Envirite13240.36,EnvironmentalConsultants5229.87,Smiley2214.23,FrankiesSeptic163.80,CityCadillac40.20,Nelson5769.08,LeoIngrahamJr1310.40,CECOS17388.00. City $40.20 has no service description: not a leachate invoice. EPA/TAT table subtotal14,778.80; its line items total14,780.56 (3362.44+2140.95+36.26+8589.15+650).
- p11 Table4 totals $156,821.58 using142,041.02+14,780.56. Thus total discrepancy$650 and subtotal discrepancy$1.76; retain both, request invoices/obligation ledger rather than invent reconciliation. July6,1983 CityHall1300hrs meeting chaired OSC KenBanaszek and DonRenny, CadillacUtilities. Wastes/sewer removed and building secured; contaminated soil explicitly remains.
- p12: PRP notices and opportunity to perform cleanup, ownership/bankruptcy chronology; no contacted PRP undertook removal. EPA/MDNR roles. Named recipients are not a fresh adjudicated-liability conclusion.
- p13: federal/contractor actions; weather delays; sewer removed July27,1983; unsealed catch basin functioned as dry well. p14: unsealed drain tiles and indoor catch basins, discolored soil. Under-building groundwater contamination described as probable, not confirmed sampling.

### Tie-backs and boundaries

OSC pp7,13 explicitly date the removal to1983; RI p25 retrospectively dates similar removal actions to1982. OSC p4 says operations began1971; RI p25 says1972. Preserve differences. Existing1985progress report broadens groundwater investigation;1986work plan proposes further work;1988RI is historical VOC/chromium investigation. None establishes a PFAS source-to-Plett pathway. Separate2020LDFAminutes discuss Northernaire closeout and a reported PFAS-test requirement, but no blanket completion inference.

## Cadillac RI, August1988 FINAL DRAFT —169 supplied pages

pp1–9 cover/contents: listed references,Plate1,appendicesA–S not supplied. pp10–15 executive summary:5known/probable sources,7plumes,3sand aquifers/2clay aquitards,limiteddeepdata. pp16–31 history, contracts, geography, industrial and remedial history, climate and receiving waters. p25 history differs fromOSC as above. p31 ClamRiver receivesWWTPeffluent; not proof that every plume enters that outfall.

pp32–37 field/sampling/aquifer-test methods; pp38–50 period-specific ARAR review; p45 surface-water table prints MERRIMAC RIVER although surrounding report concerns Cadillac/ClamRiver: template/discrepancy flag, not a Michigan river identification. pp51–63 surveys, borings, geology, maps/cross-sections. pp64–67 Kysor residualsoil and1981excavation. pp68–82 construction methods, synoptic levels, gradients, permeability and model. pp83–97 laboratory/data-validation methods and analytical plume interpretation. pp98–106 conceptual model, uncertainties and future remedial context. pp107–167 baseline risk evaluation, old toxicology/regulatory assumptions, hypothetical receptors, predictive modeling, ecological lists, calculation tables and uncertainties. pp168–169 glossary ends file; no referenced appendices follow.

Specific supported checks:

- pp58–59 well-sorted,well-rounded fine/medium quartz/feldspar sand,usually<3%fines,locally17%;USCSSP. Upper aquitard variable0–30%silt,clay22ftnearSLW12/thin2ftNorthernaire; sands/gravel do not imply uniform permeability. Sixth/Leeson pond retained water above clay while13thStreet pond infiltrated rapidly.
- pp57,60–63: interpreted pinch-outs; lower clay–sand–clay sequence; MB4 upperclay absent, bottomclay only3ft. Wideboring spacing limits horizontal continuity assessment. Dashed contacts/questionmarks are interpretations, not complete subsurface mapping.
- p65 map locates1981Kysor excavation and KBborings; pp66–67 measured soilconcentrations/residual leaching. No PFAS panel.
- p70 generic monitoring-well construction,7.5inboring,2inIDgalvanizedriser,5ftstainlessscreen,grout,naturalsandpack. p71 P3at13th/Plett,P4airport,P5PleasantLake are level-only piezometers,not PFASsamplewells.
- p72 levelsdatedJune29,1987 except P3–5Aug21. SLW36 prints1291.74 vs1271.74inTable5-3p80; preserve discrepancy. p73 July29 narrative vsJune29table/map also unresolved. NS notsurveyed, dashesnodata, notzero.
- p76 Keck permeability32wells: shallow0.003–0.058cm/s; intermediate0.026–0.079cm/s. AppendixN absent. p80all16pairedgradientsdownward;5x10^-4/9x10^-4 entries visually confirmed. This is historical hydraulic evidence, not a PFAS transit measurement.
- pp74,77,78 arrows are historical gradient interpretations. p78 uses three loweraquiferwells only. pp75,98 average watermovement~200ft/yrshallow and80intermediate, not a modern contaminant-specific arrivaltime.
- pp85–86shallow/intermediateVOCmaps and pp92,95–96plumeprofiles use historical concentrations. Small overlappedwell IDs, pointvalues (especiallyp53) remain incompletelylegible; don't extract guessed values. p86mixesMay/Junedata withfiveAugustwell results as legendnotes.
- p93 tentative~4ppbdeepMRWTCE belowreporting limit considered likely samplecarryover after highconcentrationSLW50;blankMV115TCEsupports concern. Do not label as confirmed deepaquifercontamination.
- p94 CrVIattributedNorthernaire,limitedthinintermediateplume. VOCsourceoverlap and FourWinns/Ingraham attributionuncertainty pp89–91 retained.
- pp110–111frequency/maxima are measured analytical summaries; later tables are exposurecalculations. Chromium10/24max773ppb;TCE31/43Rexairmax153000ppb. No PFAS information. p122historical toxicitycoefficients,notcurrentmedicalguidance.
- p124/127 oldARAR values; p131hypotheticalreceptorsR1–R6notactualsamplepoints. pp130–135 futurearrival dates are model predictions. ModelappendicesR/Sabsent, cannot independently reproduce. p1371980census10199 notcontemporarypopulation. p142plantsobserved;pp144–145mammals/birdsexpected fromhabitat,references notobservedinventory.
- pp149–162 old riskmath tables contrast child/adult/mostprobable/realisticworstcase. WindowsOCR fails manydensecells; imagelegibility insufficient to strictly verify everyexponent. No new numericriskclaims promoted. p156clearly assumes100ug/LTCE,2L/day,70kg,365days/year,70yearsexposure→3.14e-5risk; this is a scenario,notactualwellmeasurement. p162futureCrVI295/122/600ug/L scenarios and1.69/.70/3.43 ratios similarlyhypothetical.
- pp163–164 explicitly discuss over/underestimation, omittedexposureroutes, assumed absorption/lifetime and limiteddata. Conclusions do not diagnose actualpersons/current exposure.

## Open original-record leads

1. OSCp3,6–14 → absentAppendicesI(manifests),P(photographs),Q(inventory/analyticalresults),cost/obligationfiles andotherlistedappendices. Needed to reconcile totals, confirmtablemanifestnumbers andunderlying cleanupdata.
2. OSCp10CityCadillac$40.20 → contractorinvoice/servicevoucher; unknownservice. Do notclassifyasleachatepayment.
3. OSCp12unnamedlocallandfill → actualdisposalmanifest; noWexfordidentificationyet.
4. RIpp3–9 → references/Plate1/AppendicesA–S,particularlyNhydraulicmethods,Oanalyticalvalidation,R/Smodeldetails. Neededforcompletepackageandmodelverification.
5. RIpp53,72,80 → higherqualityoriginalmonitorwellplan/surveylevels toresolveillegibleIDs andSLW36elevationconflict.

Publication scope: one new OSC original; one catalog entry for already-public RI original; enrich existing license/draft descriptions and timeline boundaries; one1983cleanupblock.
